question: What curved spacetime really means

scene.title: What curved spacetime really means
scene.subtitle: Straight paths that start side by side don’t stay side by side. That is what curved spacetime means, and it explains the tides.
scene.takeaway: Spacetime is curved where floating paths that start side by side come together or spread apart. Mass makes the paths around it come together.

beats.title: Straight lines that meet
beats.body: Two walkers start side by side on a ball, facing the same way, and walk straight ahead. Neither ever turns, yet they get closer and meet. On a curved surface, straight paths that start parallel come together.

beats.title: Falling side by side
beats.body: Now let go of two balls side by side, high above the Earth. Neither is pushed, and at first neither moves at all. In empty space they would stay the same distance apart forever. Near Earth they drift together, like the walkers: that is curved spacetime.

beats.title: Around the Earth
beats.body: Now let go of a ring of balls all around the Earth. The whole ring shrinks: the Earth’s mass makes floating paths around it come together. Standing on the ground means being held off those paths: that is the push you feel as your weight.

beats.title: Tides
beats.body: Away from the Earth, float with one ball inside a small ring. The nearest ball speeds up a little more and the farthest a little less. So the ring stretches, while its sides draw in. With no mass inside, it doesn’t simply shrink. The Moon stretches Earth’s oceans the same way, into two bulges.
